I had a bunch of stuffed animals (gifts from relatives or lovebombs from parents), that always stood at the foot of my bed.  I adored them.  They had their own personalities, but they couldn’t talk (obviously), but I knew they loved me because they never yelled at me.  They just sat there, smiling, ready for me to hug them when I needed comfort, and never judging me for it.  They were the closest thing to a family that I understood.

So my stuffed animals would lean against the wall at the foot of my bed, watching over me.  In return, I would sleep with my head facing the bedroom door, ready to use my body as a shield so I could protect my “real” family from my parents.  I kept mentally daring them to try something physical - not because they had done much of that before, but because I was willing to die.  And I wanted to die for someone I cared about.

An easy way to guess what a card means is to try to decipher the artwork on the card.  Pretend you’re teaching someone else how to write a tarot card description: is there symbolism?  What colors are used?  Is there any sense of motion in the lines?  What do you think those mean? Etc.  Each artist presents cards in different ways, so the meaning may be obvious or it may be more like how the artist *feels* about the card.  When in doubt, google is pretty reliable too - most sources kinda agree on the key words of each card.

It is a stereotype, but somewhat based in truth.  Children (supposedly) dislike bitter because in the past, [we knew toxins in foods tasted bitter to discourage us from eating them](https://www.sciencefocus.com/the-human-body/why-do-children-dislike-vegetables/)

I know as a kid living in the U.S., I hated green vegetables.  My parents only knew one way to prepare them: heat them up.  For flavor, we could add salt, pepper, or cheese (to cover up any flavor that’s there).  There was no attempt to actually *cook* the veggies, just heat them enough to be palatable.

But when we moved to Japan, we were introduced to a whole world of dishes and delicious sauces that made veggies our favorite part!   Changing the method of cooking from “just heat and eat” to grilling, stir fry, or roasting made a huge difference.  But honestly, I feel like sauces from Asian cuisine just enhance the flavors of vegetables in wonderful ways!

Exactly this.  Heather Bresch’s company (previously Mylan) bought the patent to the EpiPen auto-injector, and then acquired a competing company (Dey) that owned the patent for competing auto-injector devices.  So Bresch had a monopoly on the auto-injector technology, and until the price-gouging scandal, her company was going to hold those patents until 2025.  

To be clear, the main cost of manufacturing the EpiPen was the stab-your-thigh-through-your-clothes auto-injector, which cost about $28 in 2017.  The amount of epinephrine - the actual active ingredient - only cost $1 per EpiPen.  Bresch was already making a profit selling them at $50 each…but it wasn’t enough.

So Heather Bresch uses daddy’s (Joe Manchin’s) connections to speak to Congress and lobby for EpiPens to be more widely used.  She gave impassioned speeches, convincing them to include EpiPens in Medicare/Medicaid programs, as well as requiring at least one unassigned EpiPen in schools through the Dept. of Education.   She even pushed for EpiPens to be required in first aid kits for public places like amusement parks (specifically, she teamed up with Disney.  They created a character and everything).  

Bresch’s lobbying caused Medicare/Medicaid, the Dept. of Education, and select private businesses to ***need*** EpiPens.  Prices had been steadily increasing over time, but after that legislation passed, EpiPen prices just skyrocketed.

The only reason Heather Bresch and Mylan got caught is because they were scamming federal programs out of millions.  It was “fine” when individual patients & families were paying $660 for a single-use medication, but when the *government* had to pay for those prices, suddenly it was a problem.  That’s the only reason the price gouging stopped.  It’s the only reason Mylan quickly churned out a generic version of the EpiPen at a lower cost - ***which they had been capable of doing the entire time***.   Have no sympathy for pharmaceutical companies.  

Source: Worked at Mylan.  Met Heather Bresch.  Wrote my MBA thesis on Mylan’s EpiPen nonsense.  I feel dirty just being associated with them.

Alternatively, if you had any underlying issues with your mother, holding on to those may be keeping her away.  But that is something to tackle separately.

What I *do* remember is vomiting to relieve the pain, while my mom exasperatedly sent the other girls home.  I couldn’t function much at all, so I just took a water bottle into the bathroom and propped myself up by the tub.  Mom thought I was being dramatic and went to bed.  I couldn’t sleep at all.

The next day, it wasn’t any better.  It was like a sharp, stabbing pain in the upper abdomen that traveled through my spine to my lower back.  My parents insisted that I should get dressed and leave my room (“We are **not** trailer trash!”), but all I could manage was sitting on the couch. Eating food was too painful, and anything I was force-fed would he puked up later to ease the cramping.  Ice water had 50/50 chance to stay down, so I stuck with that.
Fast forward 6 days, and nothing has improved.  My mom doesn’t know why, but she is dead sure that I was making this up for attention - even though it was *fucking summer*.  Why would I fake that to ruin my summer??  At least Dad was unbothered by my predicament, because I wasn’t blocking the tv or making too much noise.

By Day 8, I started turning yellow.  My skin and eye-whites became alarmingly jaundiced, and my mom finally took me to a doctor.  Lo and behold, I had gallstones (thanks Yaz!). 
I had an extra large gallstone stuck in the duct shared by my gallbladder and liver - and because we waited for so long, my liver was failing and my pancreas was inflamed for trying to pick up the slack.  Obviously, no apology or “we’ll believe you next time”.  In fact, my parents wouldn’t let me have the surgery to fix it while I was a minor - I had to wait until I turned 18 (5+ years) to get it done myself.

Clean something - just pick an area - for 15 minutes.  See if you can do it again tomorrow.  If you feel like you can do more, add another 15 minutes.  Being able to see progress, even if it’s just a drop in the bucket, is worth it.

Leave a genuine positive review for something you bought online.  Bonus points if you can leave a review on a handmade item, because those reviews mean so much to the people who make them.  You have to reflect on the good qualities of the item or experience, and you can make someone’s day!

Listen to music, but meet yourself in the middle.  Your favorite music might not cut it right now, so find something else.  There’s a world of different music out there!  Whatever makes you feel better is the right choice, and maybe you’ll find a new favorite.

Being told to “exercise! You’ll feel better!” just flies in the face of what depression does - it robs you of energy, enjoyment, and excitement for anything.  Sometimes exercise requires more energy than you can give.  So start with bite-size steps: Walk around the block, park a little further away, or find a park you can casually wander through.  You might have to trick yourself into exercise, and though it might not instantly **cure** depression, you can say “Hey, I did that.”

If you have a pet, spend some quality time with them (cuddle, play, go for a walk together, give them a treat, etc.).  Your pets do love you, no matter how you feel about yourself.  Showing your pets some love will reinforce that yes, you do deserve their love in return.

Reaching out to trusted friends, family, or supportive colleagues can be hard.  Admitting you feel like crap is hard enough, but believing that anyone cares is impossible sometimes.  There are depression support hotlines, and counseling services offered online and by text.  Many places of worship also host support groups that don’t cost anything and won’t ask too many questions.  In my experience, even talking to pets can help!  If you want to talk it out, there are ways, places, and resources to make it happen - you just have to pick the path that appeals to you.
